transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Leaders of the world's most advanced economies, the G7, say they will coordinate to release
100 million barrels of crude oil over the next four months, including a substantial
release of diesel fuel within the first 20 days.
This in an effort to stabilize prices and ensure supply, NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports
French President Emmanuel Macron call the G7 meeting following pressure from the Trump
administration.
President Trump had threatened to stop exports of U.S. diesel entirely in an attempt to lower
U.S. prices ahead of the midterm elections.
French President Emmanuel Macron has previously said such a move would be a catastrophe.
European governments are also under huge pressure from their populations as the price of gas
and diesel skyrockets.
The G7 leaders said they agreed on the coordinated measures that would help stabilize energy
supplies, shield households and businesses from price shocks, and strengthen the long-term
resilience of global energy systems.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
The governor of New York, supporting state Attorney General Letitia James to oversee
the investigation into an alleged gang rape at a Cornell University fraternity house two
years ago.
On NPR's Here Now, former federal prosecutor Moira Penza lays out what she hopes the state
AG examines.
Well, if I were Letitia James, I'm going to be looking not only at whether these charges
should be brought, but what were the failures two years ago and making sure that we don't
repeat those failures.
So now you're going to want to be interviewing witnesses, putting them before a grand jury,
applying for search warrants for electronic records, and subpoenaing all of the information
obtained by Cornell as part of the Title IX investigation.
At a news conference today, the New York AG said she was focused on the criminal investigation,
not on the actions of the Tompkins County District Attorney criticized for failing to
thoroughly investigate the case.
The accuser identified as Jane Doe filed a lawsuit last month naming, among others, Cornell,
IFI fraternity, and seven of its members.
The administration has begun mailing $500 checks to some Americans who bought health
insurance through the Affordable Care Act, and Paris Windsor-Johnson has more on the payments
and who qualifies.
Only a million people in 30 states are receiving the payments.
There are eligible customers who bought coverage through healthcare.gov without federal help
paying their premiums.
People in states with their own insurance marketplaces are not included.
The Trump administration says the money comes from excess fees collected to run the federal
marketplace.
Insurance companies pay those fees and pass the costs along through premiums.
But health policy experts caution that a surplus doesn't necessarily mean customers were
overcharged.
The checks began going out Wednesday, along with a letter from President Trump touting
his efforts to lower healthcare costs.
Windsor-Johnson, NPR News, Washington.
It's NPR.
The United States economy added 29,000 jobs in September, marking a slowdown from August
when 133,000 jobs were added, according to today's report from the Labor Department.
The unemployment rate has ticked up to 4.2 percent.
The numbers appear to show a cooldown in the labor market, though the employment numbers
can be volatile, and this comes as the Federal Reserve has to decide later this month whether
to raise interest rates again, after doing so last month.
Russian President Vladimir Putin is warning the West against further escalating tensions
over Ukraine.
His remarks coming at a foreign policy forum outside of Moscow, NPR's Charles Maines has
the latest.
To address, Putin cast Russia as a victim of Western aggression over the years, saying
NATO had taken advantage of Russian goodwill following the breakup of the Soviet Union,
and later Putin claim forced Russian to its current war in Ukraine.
The Kremlin leader signaled that conflict would continue.
Putin effectively rejected recent U.S. proposals for Russia and Ukraine to halt strikes on
energy and shipping this winter.
He also said any future peace depended on Ukraine first surrendering additional land
Russian forces have failed to seize in more than four and a half years of war.
That demand came as he warned the West.
Moscow was ready to use its nuclear arsenal if Russia felt its own territory was ever
under threat.
Charles Maines, NPR News, Moscow.
This week, Defense Secretary Pete Hexeth said the Pentagon was opening an Office of Religious
Affairs.
The Pentagon has said the new office will not favor one faith over another.
I'm Lakshmi Singh, NPR News.

topics.text: G7 leaders agree to coordinate release of 100 million barrels of crude oil over next four months
New York Governor supports state Attorney General Letitia James overseeing Cornell University fraternity rape investigation
Trump administration begins mailing $500 checks to Americans who bought ACA health insurance without federal premium help
U.S. economy added 29,000 jobs in September; unemployment rate rises to 4.2 percent
Russian President Vladimir Putin warns West against escalating tensions over Ukraine, signals conflict will continue
Pentagon opens new Office of Religious Affairs, says office will not favor one faith over another
